paper-2607.25294.title: CLBench-V: Evaluating Multimodal Context Learning from Grounding to Knowledge Acquisition
paper-2607.25294.summary: Real-world tasks often require models to learn from task-specific context rather than relying only on pre-trained knowledge. While recent work has highlighted this capability as context learning, existing evaluations mainly focus on textual contexts.

paper-2607.25308.title: CAST: Game Solvers as Turn-Level Teachers for LLM Agents
paper-2607.25308.summary: Training large language models (LLMs) to act in long-horizon games is a promising step toward generalist decision-making, yet reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on sparse final rewards that reveal little about which decisions determi…

paper-2607.25310.title: Human-in-the-Loop Signature Bootstrapping for UAV Hyperspectral PFM-1 Mine Detection
paper-2607.25310.summary: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is useful for material discrimination, but operational mine screening also depends on how many false alarms must be inspected before targets are found.

paper-2607.25337.title: Temporal-Distance JEPA: Plan-Aware Representation Learning for Latent World Model Predictive Control
paper-2607.25337.summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn world models by predicting in representation space rather than reconstructing pixels, making them a natural backbone for latent model predictive control from offline demonstration logs.

paper-2607.25380.title: Memory for Large Language Models
paper-2607.25380.summary: Memory has evolved into a foundational architectural dimension in large language models (LLMs), shifting from an implicit byproduct of computation to a spectrum of explicit, controllable mechanisms.

paper-2607.25431.title: CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
paper-2607.25431.summary: Coding agents repeatedly search, navigate, and retain context from evolving repositories, but disconnected indexes, language servers, and task-local histories force repeated discovery and obscure lifecycle costs.

paper-2607.25537.title: Visual prompt engineering for video models
paper-2607.25537.summary: In the age of foundation models, a model is only as good as its prompt. For this reason, prompt engineering has become an essential technique for improving language model performance.

paper-2607.25565.title: ReDesign: Recovering Editable Design Structures from Images via Agentic Decomposition
paper-2607.25565.summary: Recovering an editable design file from a raster image is a common and costly bottleneck in modern design workflows, yet remains challenging since editability depends on recovering multi-modal attributes, such as typography, vector geometry, colors, grouping,…

paper-2607.25572.title: Mapping CVEs to MITRE ATT&CK Techniques: A Curated Gold-Set Classifier and the Limits of LLM-Assisted Label Expansion
paper-2607.25572.summary: We present a reproducible pipeline for mapping Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) to MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques from free-text vulnerability descriptions.

paper-2607.25659.title: CoRT: Counterfactual Replay for Token-Level Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization
paper-2607.25659.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning enriches language model training by evaluating model outputs against explicit criteria.

paper-2607.25669.title: OmniDelta: Skill-Driven Budget Allocation for Token Compression in OmniLLMs
paper-2607.25669.summary: Emerging Omni-modal Large Language Models (OmniLLMs) enable unified understanding of text, audio, and video, but their long audio-video token sequences introduce substantial memory and inference costs.

paper-2607.25675.title: DecoEvo: Score-Decoupled Co-Evolution of Solver and Rubric-Generator Skills in Text Space
paper-2607.25675.summary: Text-space optimization adapts large language models (LLMs) by editing external natural-language artifacts rather than model weights, so the optimized artifacts remain inspectable and the model can be treated as a black box.

paper-2607.25802.title: Explicit Layer Modeling for Video Object Insertion and Layer Decomposition
paper-2607.25802.summary: Most video editing systems still lack explicit layered video representations, limiting their ability to perform realistic compositing, object reuse, and consistent manipulation.

paper-2607.25857.title: Shieldstral
paper-2607.25857.summary: We introduce Shieldstral, a 3B-parameter policy-adaptive multimodal safety classifier that matches or outperforms models nearly 7times its size on text safety benchmarks and sets a new state of the art on multimodal safety classification.

paper-2607.25895.title: HiFi-UMI: Learning Deployable Manipulation Policies from High-Fidelity UMI Data Alone
paper-2607.25895.summary: Learning deployable manipulation policies is bottlenecked by the scarcity of data that is both high-fidelity and scalable.

paper-2607.25948.title: MODUS: Decoder-Only Any-to-Any Modeling of Diverse Modalities
paper-2607.25948.summary: Any-to-any models predict any modality from any combination of others within a single network, a formulation used in multimodal vision and vision-language models, and increasingly in scientific domains such as ecology and astronomy.

paper-2607.25970.title: Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization
paper-2607.25970.summary: RL for code correctness is now established: have the model generate a program, run it against hidden test cases, and reward solutions that pass. Extending this to code optimization seems straightforward: just add execution time to the reward.

paper-2607.26004.title: Parallel Decoding Distillation for Fast Image and Video Generation
paper-2607.26004.summary: Generation in video diffusion or flow models is computationally expensive due to the slow and iterative sampling process.

paper-2607.26037.title: Wonder: Video World Model Done Better
paper-2607.26037.summary: We present Wonder, a general-purpose video world model for real-time, camera-controllable world exploration.

paper-2607.26055.title: πR^2: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies
paper-2607.26055.summary: Generalist manipulation policies increasingly take the form of action-chunking flow policies built on large pretrained backbones. Such chunks run open-loop, so the policy cannot react to sensory input arriving mid-execution, sacrificing reactivity.

paper-2607.26056.title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models
paper-2607.26056.summary: Forward latent world models predict how actions change a scene, but recover actions for a desired change only through expensive test-time search.

paper-2607.26057.title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
paper-2607.26057.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) grounds token-level supervision in the student's own trajectory, yet suffers from prefix failure: once the student commits to a wrong reasoning direction, all subsequent generation builds on this deviation, producing misdirected c…

paper-2607.26115.title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale
paper-2607.26115.summary: We introduce GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming agent that is trained to discover novel prompt injection attacks against frontier LLMs. The goal of this model is to evaluate and improve the robustness of our production systems.

paper-2607.26314.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents
paper-2607.26314.summary: Stealth, the discipline of achieving an objective without revealing your presence, capabilities, or collected intelligence, is what separates sophisticated operators from detectable ones.

paper-2607.26410.title: Voice Memory for Agentic Speech Recognition
paper-2607.26410.summary: We present Voice Memory, a inference-only scheme for agentic speech recognition: at stream time, a frozen corrector reads a single per-domain memory.md and decides per utterance whether to act on the hypothesis or abstain and keep the 1-best.

paper-2607.26497.title: BM25 Wins at Scale: A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms
paper-2607.26497.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) spans lexical and dense retrieval, graph-based indexing, and agentic search, but these paradigms are usually evaluated on different benchmarks at one corpus size, leaving their accuracy-cost scaling unclear.

paper-2607.26627.title: Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes
paper-2607.26627.summary: Speculative Decoding (SD) accelerates large language model inference by allowing a lightweight draft model to propose tokens that are subsequently verified in parallel by a larger target model.

paper-2607.26637.title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability
paper-2607.26637.summary: Deployed LLM agents increasingly keep their long-term memory as a filesystem: a directory tree of markdown files that the agent itself reads, writes, and reorganizes through generic file tools.

paper-2607.26754.title: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation
paper-2607.26754.summary: Recent game world models can generate visually realistic and interactive environments conditioned on player actions.

paper-2607.26760.title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model
paper-2607.26760.summary: Recent advances in AI agents have increasingly internalized native capabilities into their underlying foundation models, giving rise to multimodal foundation models and large reasoning models.

paper-2607.26769.title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?
paper-2607.26769.summary: Multimodal large language models increasingly use sketches, annotations, tools, and intermediate images during reasoning, but it remains unclear whether they truly rely on these visual states.

paper-2607.26784.title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution
paper-2607.26784.summary: Large language model agents often encounter related yet distinct tasks that share reusable solution patterns.

paper-2607.26791.title: SecRespond: Benchmarking AI Agents for Real-World Post-Compromise Incident Response
paper-2607.26791.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly adopted in real-world security operations with access to host artifacts and command-line interfaces (CLIs), making it critical to thoroughly assess their security capabilities.

paper-2607.26811.title: DistillAlign: Coordinating Mode Covering and Mode Seeking in Autoregressive Video Distillation
paper-2607.26811.summary: Existing autoregressive video distillation methods commonly adopt a Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD)-based multi-stage pipeline.

paper-2607.27146.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
paper-2607.27146.summary: Coding agents have made substantial progress on software engineering tasks that modify existing codebases, including bug fixing and feature implementation.

paper-2607.27155.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
paper-2607.27155.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to assist users in completing tasks. However, existing benchmarks provide limited support for evaluating whether agents can carry out office-suite workflows at a reasonable cost.

paper-2607.27167.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
paper-2607.27167.summary: LLM-based agents excel at software engineering tasks where an existing codebase provides context, but constructing a program from scratch remains fundamentally harder.

paper-2607.27180.title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?
paper-2607.27180.summary: Evaluating whether a vision-language model (VLM) can act through a physical body is challenging. The outcome of an action couples the VLM's decision with motor control.

paper-2607.27191.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
paper-2607.27191.summary: Forecasts of explosive AI progress hinge on AI agents automating AI research. But evidence on whether agents can carry out open-ended AI research is thin.

paper-2607.27205.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
paper-2607.27205.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models commonly adopt an LLM-centric V to L to A pathway, where visual observations are projected into the representation space of a large language model before being decoded into robot actions.

paper-2607.27230.title: Multi-Head Attention Residuals
paper-2607.27230.summary: Transformers propagate information across depth through a single additive residual stream: every sublayer reads only the most recent state. Attention residuals relax this by letting each sublayer attend, through a learned softmax.

paper-2607.27278.title: OVEarth-Bench: Evaluating Category Breadth and Query Diversity for Open-Vocabulary Earth Observation
paper-2607.27278.summary: Open-vocabulary Earth observation (EO) aims to localize geospatial concepts specified in natural language rather than a fixed label set. Existing benchmarks, however, usually cover narrow category vocabularies or limited query forms.

paper-2607.27372.title: Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation
paper-2607.27372.summary: The deep learning revolution, kicked off by AlexNet, taught us that end-to-end training beats decomposing a problem into hand-designed stages.

paper-2607.27380.title: VideoCoCo: Code-as-CoT for Physically-Consistent Video Generation via an Agentic Dual-Engine System
paper-2607.27380.summary: Text-to-video models have achieved remarkable visual quality, yet they still struggle to generate physically consistent dynamics because the temporal evolution of a scene must be inferred implicitly from a highly compressed text prompt.

paper-2607.27616.title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing
paper-2607.27616.summary: Text-to-image and personalized editing models now synthesize high-fidelity single-subject images with ease.

paper-2607.27652.title: Harness-G: A Graph-Structured Harness for Search Agents
paper-2607.27652.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) search agents commonly model retrieval as free-form natural-language query generation and optimize multi-turn interactions using final-answer rewards.

paper-2607.27703.title: SpatialCLI: Learning to Reason With Spatial Tools, Then Without Them
paper-2607.27703.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used in embodied agents to interpret visual inputs, reason about spatial relationships, and make task-level decisions based on that reasoning.

paper-2607.27816.title: Beyond Borrowed Histories: Person-Aligned User Simulation for Interactive Role-Playing Evaluation
paper-2607.27816.summary: Role-playing agents (RPAs) have become one of the most important consumer applications of large language models.

paper-2607.27919.title: Memory Decoder at Scale: A Pretrained, Parametric Long-Term Memory
paper-2607.27919.summary: Decoder-only language models entangle long-term memory and reasoning in a single parameter set, making it difficult to scale memory capacity independently.

paper-2607.27958.title: Σ-Mem: An Online Reliability Memory for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
paper-2607.27958.summary: Memory is central to long-horizon LLM agents, yet existing memory systems primarily preserve interaction content rather than modeling which agents can be trusted and under what conditions.

paper-2607.28022.title: Flux-OPD: On-Policy Distillation with Evolving Contexts
paper-2607.28022.summary: Large language model training in open-ended domains lacks verifiable rewards, making task preferences difficult to formalize as effective supervision.

paper-2607.28074.title: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
paper-2607.28074.summary: Computer-use agents learn from what their actions change, so training one needs applications it can act on, break and reset. The applications that matter most are login-gated and stateful, so synthetic environments stand in for them.

paper-2607.28227.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
paper-2607.28227.summary: GUI agents have the potential to become a general purpose executor over existing digital devices.

paper-2607.28272.title: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
paper-2607.28272.summary: Retrieving past experiences has become a common strategy to enhance large language model agents.

paper-2607.28308.title: Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing
paper-2607.28308.summary: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models route each token to multiple experts, suggesting a geometric account of their benefit: co-selected experts should contribute distinct representation directions.

paper-2607.28319.title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations
paper-2607.28319.summary: This work presents Fairness Pruning, a lightweight structural intervention method designed for the management and future mitigation of demographic bias in large language models (LLMs).

paper-2607.28362.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics Representations from a Video and Its Shadow
paper-2607.28362.summary: We present ShadowDancer, a novel approach to any-action, frame-level control of interactive video world models.

paper-2607.28374.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger
paper-2607.28374.summary: Multimodal agents for visual question answering increasingly operate as multi-step trajectories that interleave perception, retrieval, and reasoning, yet evaluation still largely reduces to final-answer accuracy.

paper-2607.28410.title: Can Large Language Models Execute Parent Orders?
paper-2607.28410.summary: Parent-order execution is a core problem in algorithmic trading, where the goal is to split a large order into smaller orders while reducing execution costs.

paper-2607.28509.title: RefCaptioner: Multi-Reference Image-Grounded Video Captioning
paper-2607.28509.summary: Existing video captioning models generate natural descriptions of video content but cannot explicitly ground local visual elements to multiple reference images.

paper-2607.28568.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
paper-2607.28568.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires AI systems that improve the process of building AI (i.e., AI4AI); machine learning engineering (MLE) offers a concrete, executable testbed for studying this capability.

paper-2607.28582.title: β-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
paper-2607.28582.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is a promising approach to improve reasoning language models, but it remains brittle in practice: making it work reliably often requires substantial engineering effort.

paper-2607.28595.title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
paper-2607.28595.summary: The fundamental goal of agentic visual reasoning is to improve the success rate of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on complex tasks, rather than merely equipping them with a sophisticated yet inefficient reasoning paradigm.

paper-2607.28611.title: Chimera: Designing and Chinchilla-Scaling Hybrid Visual Diffusion Transformers
paper-2607.28611.summary: Visual generation increasingly requires high-resolution images, long videos, and multimodal context, making the quadratic cost of full attention prohibitive. We introduce Chimera, a hybrid visual diffusion backbone with a principled scaling recipe.

paper-2607.28618.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
paper-2607.28618.summary: Chemistry literature synthesis often requires assembling specific findings scattered across many publications, yet existing literature-search systems primarily return ranked document lists.

paper-2607.28624.title: PhiZero: A World Model Built Around Physical Language
paper-2607.28624.summary: We introduce PhiZero, a physical world model built around physical language, a compact discrete representation of world-state transitions.

paper-2607.28625.title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
paper-2607.28625.summary: Embodied intelligence faces a fundamental data bottleneck. Models must capture how first-person perception, whole-body motion, dexterous manipulation, object state, sound, and touch evolve together as humans pursue goals over time.

paper-2607.28627.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
paper-2607.28627.summary: Long visual context poses a challenge for vision-language models: performance degrades as the number of distractors grows, and processing all tokens at once is computationally infeasible under GPU memory constraints.
